correctionToTheDispatchsOwnPremise.dispatchSaid: Real Texas district codes (C, D, E, F, GC, SF-1, MU) match nothing and all fall through to C.other.fill. They are orange because they are all classed unclassified.
correctionToTheDispatchsOwnPremise.atSource: Partly true, and the difference matters. The CODE ladder does miss everything — none of P-5/P-4/P-2/SFR/R-1/MF/COM/AG occurs in the corpus. But a DESCRIPTION keyword ladder runs underneath it and catches roughly 74% of a real Bastrop tile: 'Commercial real property' hits the 'commercial' keyword, 'Single-family residential' hits 'single', and so on.

adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.challenge: Seven land-use classes is fewer than the eight the data has. Is folding exempt a quiet quality loss?
adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.answer: It is a loss and it is stated, not quiet. The measured ceiling over the legal gamut is worst all-pairs CVD 8.9 / normal 16.9 at N=7 and 8.3 / 14.5 at N=8; the normal-vision floor is 15, so eight cannot pass. Exempt keeps a named legend row inside 'Exempt, utility and other classified'. If the operator would rather have exempt as its own hue, the trade is naming which class loses one — that is a ruling, not a lane call, and it is in the close as an open item.

adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.challenge: Minimal-hazard flood land now paints nothing. Does that read as a broken layer?
adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.answer: Mitigated three ways: the polygon keeps a hairline outline, the legend row says 'Minimal hazard — outside the mapped floodplain' and carries an explicit OUT badge, and the badge column has THREE states so 'no determination' (Zone D) never reads as 'outside'. It remains the item most worth an eyeball on a real screen, which this lane cannot do without deploying.

adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.challenge: The renderer now mounts DOM chrome (the legend). Does that collide with either app's own chrome?
adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.answer: It mounts collapsed as one small chip at left:12 bottom:52 (bottom:106 under 640px), above PE's SmartSiteBadge at bottom:12/68, and it is hidden entirely unless zoning or a flood layer is visible — which on PE cold-open means hidden, because zoning defaults OFF. It is also the residual risk I cannot close from here: position against live chrome is a screen question.

adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.challenge: Two new classifier implementations each. Is the divergence test real or decorative?
adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.answer: Real, and it needed an instrument: `map/expr-eval.js` actually EVALUATES the MapLibre expressions rather than string-matching them. It throws on any operator it does not implement, so it cannot fail open. The land-use divergence test runs 118 corpus codes through both paths; the FEMA one runs all six measured live combinations plus twelve more of the published NFHL set.

adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.challenge: Are the new tests actually enforced, or are they a guardrail nobody runs?
adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.answer: They were NOT enforced. No workflow ran `pnpm --filter @hauska/map-renderer test` — the package's node:test suite had never been a CI gate, so every guard already in it was decorative. Added as a step in command-center-ci.yml, which already triggers on packages/map-renderer/**. Found by asking the question, not by the suite failing.

adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.challenge: Did anything else change that the dispatch did not ask for?
adversarialReviewOfTheBuild.answer: Three things, all named: the CC test correction above; the CI step above; and a data-driven `line-width` on the FEMA layer (severity-weighted), which is how zone identity survives a fill capped at 20% opacity over imagery. ROLE_BUDGET was NOT touched — no opacity constant was raised anywhere.

backlogFindingsNotFixedHere.finding: the `meshMode && layerKey === 'parcel-polygon'` branch does `fillOpacityExpr(layerKey, true) * saturation`, unguarded. That call returns a MapLibre `case` ARRAY for parcel-polygon, so the multiply yields NaN and setPaintProperty receives NaN. The two neighbouring branches DO guard with `typeof baseOpacity === 'number'`.
